wiki_text: Singapore's government approved Singapore LNG Corp (SLNG) to develop, own and operate the nation's second LNG terminal on 25 October 2023, announced by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong at SLNG's 10th-anniversary event. The facility is planned as an FSRU-based import terminal of up to 5 mtpa. On 23 October 2024 SLNG signed agreements to advance the project: it chartered a newbuild floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) — 200,000 m3 storage capacity, 5 mtpa regasification, to be built by Hanwha Ocean — from a subsidiary of Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL); awarded the Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) for the onshore connecting infrastructure to a subsidiary of Wood plc (FEED expected to complete around mid-2025, with an EPC RFP to follow); and partnered with Jurong Port. The terminal is targeted to be operational by the end of the decade (around 2029-2030), raising SLNG's combined LNG throughput capacity to up to 15 mtpa alongside the existing Jurong Island terminal.
